records.title: Binance Hack: $6.3B Drained on 9 Chains, $2.7B Frozen
records.summary: Bitquery says 17 Binance hot wallets on nine chains were drained between 20:04 and 23:56 UTC on October 29, and each drained wallet carries a Binance Proof-of-Reserves label in its address data. This includes five XRPL accounts that sent approximately 233.5M XRP to rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx at 20:04 UTC. At its October 30 06:43 UTC holdings read, the XRP receiver still held approximately 233.5M XRP and had made no outgoing transaction. Bitquery explicitly says the XRP Ledger receiver shares no address with the rest of the attack; it is linked by timing, transfer construction and Binance's aggregate total. On Ethereum, Bitquery lists 0x8532fa14acaf483729c449b8458aeddb900543d4 holding 197,460 ETH at 06:43 UTC, while 0x5227... held 3 ETH plus frozen stablecoins and had sent its ETH to another stash at 05:15 UTC. Its transaction history was read through approximately 02:10 UTC on Ethereum and 02:40 UTC on other chains, with later holdings read at 06:43 UTC.
records.methodology: Bitquery reports matching large on-chain drains against Binance wallet address labels, following transfers hop-by-hop, reading freeze events and chain balances. It states dollar values use prices at transfer time and holdings were read at 06:43 UTC.
records.limitations: Provider-labelled Binance PoR matches are not an independent re-parse of Binance's raw downloadable reserve export or a same-time customer-liability proof. Data is stale after 06:43 UTC. Bitquery does not identify who asked Binance's system to sign. Its Ethereum and XRP wallet clusters have no shared address; common beneficial ownership is unknown.
